**Stepwise Execution Report**

**GenAI-Driven MIL/HIL Verification Framework for Adaptive Cruise Control — PoC-1 (MPC Baseline)**

_Prepared for: Dr. Nitish Katal, Assistant Professor, School of Electronics Engineering (SENSE), VIT Chennai_

# 0\. Purpose and Scope

This report documents the complete, stepwise execution procedure for PoC-1: a GenAI-driven framework that automatically generates MIL and HIL test artifacts from formalized requirements, and validates the MathWorks MPC-based Adaptive Cruise Control (mpcACCsystem) controller against them. It consolidates the architecture, the execution steps, the technical specification of every subcomponent, success criteria, risks, deliverables, and the roadmap into a single reference document.

The controller under test in PoC-1 is the MPC baseline only. The framework is deliberately built behind a fixed Controller Abstraction Layer so that a later PoC (RL controller) can be validated by the same framework, unchanged — that forward path is summarized in Section 10 but is out of scope for PoC-1 execution.

# 1\. Objectives

- Formalize the ACC controller's behavioral requirements once, in EARS syntax, as the single source of truth for verification.
- Use a GenAI (LLM) pipeline to parse each requirement and automatically generate the MATLAB/Simulink Test code needed for MIL and HIL, removing hand-written test authoring from the critical path.
- Execute the generated tests against the MPC baseline at both MIL (normal-mode simulation) and HIL (real-time target) and confirm behavioral and timing equivalence between the two stages.
- Produce a full requirement↔test↔result traceability matrix and benchmarking report automatically, as evidence of coverage.
- Build the Controller Abstraction Layer so that this entire pipeline is reusable, unmodified, once the MPC controller is later replaced with a Reinforcement-Learning policy.

# 3\. Toolchain and Environment

| **Component**                                                 | **Role**                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| MATLAB / Simulink + Model Predictive Control Toolbox          | Hosts the mpcACCsystem baseline controller                                |
| Simulink Test (sltest.\*)                                     | MIL/HIL test sequences, assessments, Test Manager                         |
| Requirements Toolbox (slreq.\*)                               | EARS requirement authoring and traceability linking                       |
| Simulink Real-Time                                            | HIL execution target (virtual/local target for PoC-1)                     |
| Embedded Coder                                                | Available for an optional SIL equivalence check (not a PoC-1 deliverable) |
| Simulink Coverage                                             | Optional structural coverage evidence (MC/DC)                             |
| Anthropic API (Claude), called via MATLAB webwrite/weboptions | GenAI requirement parsing and test-code generation                        |

# 4\. Requirement Set (EARS)

| **ID**      | **Requirement**                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ACC-REQ-001 | While D_rel ≥ D_safe, the ACC system shall operate in speed control mode and track V_set.                                                       |
| ACC-REQ-002 | While D_rel < D_safe, the ACC system shall operate in spacing control mode and regulate the ego vehicle to maintain D_safe.                     |
| ACC-REQ-003 | The safe distance shall be computed as D_safe = D_default + T_gap × V_ego (D_default = 10 m, T_gap = 1.4 s).                                    |
| ACC-REQ-004 | Ego acceleration shall be constrained to \[-3, 2\] m/s² at all times, regardless of controller mode or implementation.                          |
| ACC-REQ-005 | On a lead-vehicle deceleration that would breach D_safe, the system shall switch to spacing control mode within one sample period (Ts = 0.1 s). |

# 5\. Stepwise Execution Procedure

![](data:image/png;base64,)

_Fig. 3 — The eight execution steps. Steps 3, 4, and 6 (orange) are where the GenAI pipeline does the work._

## Step 1 — Environment Setup and Baseline Validation

Install the toolchain (Section 3) and confirm the reference model's behavior before any GenAI artifact is introduced — this run is the golden reference that generated MIL tests must reproduce.

```
openExample('mpc/AdaptiveCruiseControlExample')
mdl = 'mpcACCsystem'; open_system(mdl);
Ts = 0.1; T = 80;
G_ego = tf(1,[0.5,1,0]);
x0_lead = 50; v0_lead = 25; x0_ego = 10; v0_ego = 20;
t_gap = 1.4; D_default = 10; v_set = 30;
amin_ego = -3; amax_ego = 2;
sim(mdl); mpcACCplot(logsout, D_default, t_gap, v_set);
```

Also set the GenAI API credential once, as an environment variable (never hard-coded):

```
setenv('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY','<key>');
```

## Step 2 — Requirement Authoring and Import

Create a Requirements Toolbox project and enter ACC-REQ-001…005 (Section 4) in EARS form. Tag each requirement with a custom attribute verification_stage = {MIL, HIL} — this is what the GenAI generator reads to know which artifacts to produce for that requirement.

```
reqProj = slreq.new('ACC_Requirements');
reqs = slreq.import('ACC_requirements_source.docx', 'Parent', reqProj);
% or author directly: slreq.createRequirement(...) per ACC-REQ-00x
```

## Step 3 — GenAI Requirement Parsing

Each requirement is sent to the LLM with a system prompt constraining the output to a strict JSON schema (the Test-Intent object). This is the artifact both the MIL and the HIL generator will consume, guaranteeing they test the same thing.

```
function intent = genai_parse_requirement(reqText, reqID)
  sysPrompt = ['Extract a strict JSON object with fields: signals_in, ', ...
    'signals_out, trigger_condition, expected_response, tolerance, ', ...
    'units, applicable_mode, timing_constraint_s. Return ONLY JSON.'];
  body = struct('model','claude-sonnet-4-6','max_tokens',1000, ...
    'system',sysPrompt,'messages',{{struct('role','user','content',reqText)}});
  opts = weboptions('HeaderFields', ...
    {'x-api-key', getenv('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'); ...
     'anthropic-version','2023-06-01'; 'content-type','application/json'}, ...
    'MediaType','application/json','Timeout',60);
  resp = webwrite('https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages', body, opts);
  intent = jsondecode(resp.content(1).text); intent.reqID = reqID;
end
```

Run this for all five requirements and store the resulting intent(1..5) array — the shared input to Steps 4 and 6.

## Step 4 — GenAI MIL Test Generation

A second LLM call, prompted to emit a Simulink Test-compatible MATLAB script from the Test-Intent JSON, targeting normal-mode simulation against the Controller Abstraction Layer's signal names. Every generated file is dry-run/lint-checked (checkcode) before being added to the Test Manager — treated as a reviewable artifact, never auto-merged.

```
% Generated MIL test — ACC-REQ-001 — Speed control mode tracking
testCase = sltest.testmanager.TestFile('ACC_REQ001_MIL.mldatx');
seq = sltest.testsequence('mpcACCsystem/Test Sequence');
seq.addStep('InitialGap', 'Amplitude = 100');  % keeps D_rel >= D_safe

simOut = sim('mpcACCsystem');
V_ego  = simOut.logsout.getElement('V_ego').Values.Data;
V_set  = v_set * ones(size(V_ego));
err    = abs(V_ego(end-50:end) - V_set(end-50:end));
assert(all(err < 0.5), 'ACC-REQ-001 FAILED: V_ego did not track V_set');
```

## Step 5 — MIL Execution

Import all generated MIL artifacts into Simulink Test Manager, link each to its requirement via Requirements Toolbox, and run the suite against the MPC baseline sitting behind the Controller Abstraction Layer.

```
testFileMIL = sltest.testmanager.TestFile('ACC_MIL_Suite.mldatx');
slreq.createLink(testFileMIL.getTestSuites.getTestCase('ACC-REQ-001'), reqs(1));
resultsMIL = sltest.testmanager.run(testFileMIL);
```

Optional: run a structural coverage pass to confirm the generated stimuli actually exercise both speed-control and spacing-control paths.

```
covOut = sim('mpcACCsystem','CovParameter','on','CovMetricStructuralLevel','MCDC');
cvhtml('ACC_Coverage_Report', covOut.CovData);
```

## Step 6 — GenAI HIL Test Generation

The same Test-Intent JSON is re-prompted with an HIL-specific system instruction: map contract signals to the target's I/O (or a virtual/local target for PoC-1), fix the real-time step at Ts = 0.1 s, and add a target-side assessment since the host cannot block on the real-time step. A companion timing assertion (worst-case execution time per Ts) is generated alongside the functional one — a missed real-time deadline is itself a failure, not just a performance number.

```
% Generated HIL test — retargeted from the same Test-Intent as MIL
tg = slrealtime('TargetPC1');           % virtual/local target for PoC-1
rtApp = slbuild('mpcACCsystem','SLRealTimeTarget');
load(tg, rtApp); start(tg);
pause(T);   % run the 80 s scenario in real time
stop(tg);
logsout_HIL = getFileScopeData(tg, 'V_ego', 'D_rel', 'WCET');
assert(all(logsout_HIL.WCET.Data < Ts), 'Real-time deadline missed');
```

## Step 7 — HIL Execution

Run the HIL suite through Test Manager exactly as MIL was run in Step 5, and numerically diff the two runs — this MIL/HIL equivalence check is the strongest evidence that the abstraction layer is doing its job.

```
resultsHIL = sltest.testmanager.run(testFileHIL);
maxDrift = max(abs(V_ego_MIL - V_ego_HIL));
assert(maxDrift < 1e-2, 'MIL/HIL behavioral drift exceeds tolerance');
```

## Step 8 — Traceability, Benchmarking and Reporting

Aggregate both suites, export the pass/fail report, and generate the requirement traceability matrix.

```
sltest.testmanager.report([resultsMIL resultsHIL], ...
    'PoC1_MPC_Verification_Report.pdf', ...
    'Title','PoC-1 — GenAI-Generated MIL/HIL Verification (MPC Baseline)');
slreq.generateReport(reqProj, 'ReportType','Traceability', ...
    'OutputFile','ACC_Traceability_Matrix.html');
```

# 6\. Subcomponent Technical Reference

## 6.1 Requirements Layer

- Tool: Requirements Toolbox (slreq.\*).
- Format: EARS (trigger / condition / expected response), one requirement per behavioral rule.
- Custom attribute: verification_stage = {MIL, HIL} per requirement, read by the GenAI generator.
- Output artifact: .reqx project, plus auto-created traceability links to every generated test case.

## 6.2 GenAI Engine

- Model: Claude (claude-sonnet-4-6), called from MATLAB via webwrite/weboptions over the standard /v1/messages endpoint.
- Stage A — Parser: requirement text → structured Test-Intent JSON (signals_in, signals_out, trigger_condition, expected_response, tolerance, units, applicable_mode, timing_constraint_s).
- Stage B — Generator: Test-Intent JSON → target-specific MATLAB/Simulink Test code (one prompt variant for MIL, one for HIL), addressed only to the Controller Abstraction Layer's signal names.
- Validation gate: every generated file is checkcode-linted and dry-run before being added to the Test Manager suite — never auto-merged.
- Reproducibility: prompt text, model version, and raw response are logged per requirement per generation.

## 6.3 Controller Abstraction Layer

- Realized as a masked Simulink subsystem with a fixed signal contract (Fig. 2): in — V_set, T_gap, V_ego, D_rel, V_rel; out — a_ego ∈ \[-3, 2\] m/s².
- PoC-1 wires the unmodified MathWorks MPC block behind this mask as the only implementation exercised.
- The mask is the only surface the GenAI pipeline and the generated tests ever reference — controller-internal parameters (MPC horizon, weights) are inaccessible to, and irrelevant for, test generation.

## 6.4 MIL Execution Layer

- Normal-mode (interpreted) Simulink simulation of mpcACCsystem, Ts = 0.1 s, scenario length T = 80 s.
- Test definition: sltest.testsequence for stimulus (e.g. lead-car profile, initial gap); sltest.assessment / assert() for the oracle.
- Aggregation: sltest.testmanager.TestFile per requirement, executed via sltest.testmanager.run().
- Optional evidence: Simulink Coverage MC/DC pass to confirm both ACC modes are exercised.

## 6.5 HIL Execution Layer

- Target: Simulink Real-Time, virtual/local target for PoC-1 (physical Speedgoat/dSPACE rig is a configuration change, not a redesign, for a later PoC).
- Real-time step fixed at Ts = 0.1 s; signals mapped from the abstraction layer's contract to target I/O (or loopback for the virtual target).
- Target-side assessment block, since the host cannot block on the real-time step; results retrieved via getFileScopeData.
- Companion timing assertion: worst-case execution time per Ts checked against the Ts budget — a hard deadline miss is a test failure.

## 6.6 Traceability and Analytics Layer

- Requirement ↔ Test ↔ Result links created via slreq.createLink at generation time, not after the fact.
- Aggregated report via sltest.testmanager.report() (PDF) and slreq's Traceability Report (HTML).
- MIL/HIL equivalence check (Step 7) is computed here and included as an explicit pass/fail line in the report, not just each stage's own result.

# 7\. Success Criteria

| **Metric**                                          | **Target**                                          |
| --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Requirements → generated, runnable MIL test         | 5 of 5, with at most 1 requiring a manual fix       |
| MIL/HIL behavioral drift (max \|V_ego\| difference) | < 1e-2 (or a documented, justified tolerance)       |
| Real-time deadline misses at HIL                    | 0                                                   |
| Traceability completeness                           | 100% of requirements linked to a MIL and a HIL test |
| Structural coverage (MC/DC) of both ACC modes       | 100%, confirming generated stimuli are non-trivial  |

# 8\. Risks and Mitigations

- Generated code doesn't compile or references the wrong signal name — mitigate with checkcode/dry-run before execution; treat as a reviewable PR.
- LLM invents a tolerance not present in the requirement — mitigate by requiring Stage A's tolerance field to be traceable to the requirement text; flag any Stage B output whose tolerance doesn't match.
- No physical HIL hardware for PoC-1 — mitigate with Simulink Real-Time's virtual/local target; document as a scope limitation, not a blocker.
- API cost/latency during iteration — cache Stage A's Test-Intent JSON per requirement; only re-run Stage B when a requirement changes.

# 9\. Deliverables Checklist

- EARS requirement set (5 requirements) in Requirements Toolbox, with traceability links
- GenAI parser and generator scripts (parser.m, generator_mil.m, generator_hil.m) with versioned prompts
- Controller Abstraction Layer: masked Simulink subsystem + interface contract document
- MIL Test Manager suite, validated against the MPC baseline
- HIL Test Manager suite (virtual/local target), validated against the same baseline
- MIL/HIL equivalence check results
- PDF verification report + HTML traceability matrix
- This execution report

# 10\. Forward Path (Out of Scope for PoC-1)

Once PoC-1 is validated, the same framework is intended to accept an RL policy behind the identical Controller Abstraction Layer (Fig. 2), with no changes to the requirements, the GenAI pipeline, or the generated MIL/HIL tests. That comparison study, and its positioning for an IEEE Transactions submission, is documented separately (see the framework approach and novelty-positioning report already on file) and is not part of PoC-1's execution or deliverables.
